how_each_number_was_obtained: For each archive, for z in min_zoom..=max_zoom and every (x, y) in raster order, ran `pmtiles tile --quiet <archive> z x y` with the pinned binary. A cell that wrote nothing is `absent`, which is how the reference reports a tile it cannot find. Each cell contributes one line, `z/x/y <sha256|absent>`, terminated by a newline; the zoom's digest is the sha256 of those lines concatenated in that order.
what_this_is: Every cell of every zoom each committed golden declares, swept through `pmtiles tile` once and reduced to one digest per zoom. tiles.json carries hand-picked rows; this carries all of them, so no future edit can narrow the coverage without changing a digest.
why_digests_and_not_rows: 44131 rows with a digest each is about 4 MB of JSON for a test repository. One digest per zoom is 3 KB and asserts the same thing. The cost is that a failure localises to a zoom, which is why `discriminating` below carries full rows for the cells a wrong tile-id convention actually moves; tests/pmtiles_sweep.rs replays them on a mismatch so the failure names a coordinate and the convention that sends the payload there. Those rows are what take the file to 66 KB.
